content_checks.claim: The image is a Commodore 64 (not VIC-20 or another Commodore model) BASIC boot screen.
content_checks.evidence: Image text reads '**** COMMODORE 64 BASIC V2 ****', '64K RAM SYSTEM  38911 BASIC BYTES FREE', 'READY.'. Wording and line order match the power-on screen on printed page 12 of the Commodore 64 User's Guide (Internet Archive commodore-64-user-guide, leaf n27).

content_checks.claim: The image is an authentic, unaltered capture of real C64 output.
content_checks.evidence: Capture method undocumented ('Own work'). Two exact colours only (digital render). Screen area measures 320 x 203 px, 3 lines more than a 25-row, 200-line text screen, which indicates cropping, editing or an inaccurate emulator. Text and layout match the real screen.
content_checks.review_question: Is a community-uploaded digital render with an undocumented capture method (and a 3-line geometry anomaly) acceptable as the 'authentic' C64 boot screen, or should a photographed real-hardware screen or a documented emulator capture be sourced instead?

content_checks.evidence: The C64 User's Guide page 12 shows the machine starting directly into COMMODORE 64 BASIC V2 at power-on. No script change needed.

content_checks.claim: SCRIPT.md:73 'When you turned on a home computer in 1982, you were usually staring at a BASIC prompt.'
content_checks.evidence: Outside this ticket's single-image scope and assigned gate. This asset only shows that the C64 powers on to a BASIC prompt; the manual scan's 1982 date comes from Internet Archive metadata (8th printing) and was not verified.
